title: Fluorescent reporter assay reveals ribonucleotides promote mismatch correction in vivo.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (1.84 MB). It is 12 figure images plus one 8-page PDF. I extracted all 8 pages of text and read Supplementary Tables S1-S3 in full: they contain exactly 170 numeric entries (the complete dataset), covering 3 reporter plasmids (GG, GG3R, GG5R) across 12 cell-line conditions with 3-9 biological replicates each. No spreadsheet, CSV, flow-cytometry file or repository deposit exists anywhere in the supplement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement ('All data are available within the manuscript and in the Supplementary File'), the assay design and cell-line genotypes, and the extra reporter variants (mPlum_GT5R, 5rC_GT, 60rC_GT, mOrange_nGG) that appear only as plotted points in figures, not as tabulated numbers.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement downloads freely without login; I opened it. But it is a PDF, not a data file, and no accession, Zenodo/Dryad record or repository deposit was found by paper_context.py.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label (reporter expression, %) is tabulated in Supplementary Tables S1-S3, so it exists as a measured value; it just has to be transcribed out of a PDF, which is effort not inference.

a3_inputs_present.note: There are no input features, only three construct names (GG, GG3R, GG5R) and a cell-line genotype label. The plasmid sequence is identical apart from one ribonucleotide position, so every example shares nearly all its sequence.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated as 'Reporter expression (%)' in every table heading and figure axis; I saw this in the PDF.

a5_enough_rows.note: I counted all 170 numbers in Tables S1-S3 by script: 3 reporters x 12 cell-line conditions x 3-9 replicates. Far under the ~400 minimum for classification, let alone 1,500 for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; the whole dataset fits in a few hundred bytes of CSV once transcribed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Replicate counts in the tables (e.g. 9 transfections for TK6 wild type) match the figure legends' 'each data point is an independent biological replicate'.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a direct physical measurement: percentage of fluorescent cells by flow cytometry, with gating shown in Supplementary Fig. S3. Not a model output.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join is possible: the data has no gene, protein, variant or compound identifier, only three in-house plasmid names and cell-line names.

controls.positive_control: The assay's own built-in control works biologically (mismatch reporters are repaired in MMR-proficient and not in MMR-deficient cells), but with 170 points there is nothing to control a model with.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: None; these reporter constructs exist only in this lab and the values are not measured anywhere else.

honest_claim_h3: At most: 'the presence and orientation of one ribonucleotide changes reporter repair by this much in these 12 cell lines' - which is the paper's own statistical result, obtainable by a t-test, not a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA around a mismatch and a cell's repair-gene status to predict how well the mismatch gets fixed.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one transfection: which reporter plasmid (mismatch type, ribonucleotide present or absent, its orientation and distance from the mismatch) and which cell line (wild type, or missing MSH2, MSH6, MLH1 or RNaseH2). I counted 170 such measurements in total.
plain_idea.predict: Percentage of cells expressing the fluorescent reporter, measured by flow cytometry 24 hours after transfection - the paper's direct read-out of mismatch correction.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs that measure DNA repair capacity in patient cells would like to know which sequence contexts are repaired well; but with 3 construct designs and 12 cell lines there is nothing for a model to learn.

ml_idea: Considered: predict mismatch-correction efficiency from reporter sequence context (ribonucleotide orientation and distance) plus host-cell repair genotype. Dead on arrival - the published data is 170 flow-cytometry percentages for 3 plasmid designs, which is a two-factor experiment, not a training set.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the whole dataset is 170 numbers in an 8-page PDF, so an hour of hand-transcription gives the complete table and no cross-validation is meaningful at that size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the numbers in Supplementary Tables S1-S3. I did: 170 measurements, 3 unique reporter designs. That kills it in five minutes.

verdict_reason: The entire dataset is 170 flow-cytometry percentages printed in an 8-page supplementary PDF: 3 reporter plasmids across 12 cell-line conditions with 3-9 replicates. A5 fails by an order of magnitude and A3 fails because there are no input features, only three construct names differing by a single ribonucleotide. This is a well-done small-scale molecular biology experiment with no ML surface at all.
